rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 5 and 6 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008, -p1-010): the prototype wins by default, but a real constraint it cannot express, naming cross-service behaviour, overrides it; which service hosts the add page and which service writes the address book is exactly that cross-service behaviour, which the single-app prototype cannot express (it keeps addresses in its own session and calls no address-book API), so the real arrangement (the INS frontend as the address book's only writer, reached through the journey handshake) stands and everything the prototype can express about the page (copy, fields, role split, buttons, messages and where each button lands) follows Design Release 2.1. DR1 made no judgement on this difference (inc-053 left it open) and Rhys's 2026-09-04 block was a deferral until the address work settled, not a judgement, so neither changes the outcome.
outcome: Keep today's handshake and the INS frontend as the address book's only writer, because where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express (ruling claim 6), while the page itself follows Design Release 2.1: 'Add a new address' still crosses to the INS frontend's /address-book/add, and when that page carries the journey handshake it shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page (caption, heading, status block, sections, fields, role split, other uses, buttons, messages, banner) and returns through the journey's /address-return to the page each button names ('Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing). In journey mode the INS add page skips 'Choose an address type' and opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the role implies, with the role's use ticked; outside a journey the address book's own add follows Design Release 2.1 in full. Same on the compose stack and in CDP; in the animals frontend's stub mode (the fit suite), where no INS frontend runs, the pickers keep showing no add link. The animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only.
